```{r setup, include=FALSE}
source_hook <- knitr::knit_hooks$get("source")
knitr::knit_hooks$set(source = function(x, options) {
  paste0(
    "\n\n<details>\n<summary>",
    options$summary,
    "</summary>\n\n",
    source_hook(x, options),
    "\n\n</details>\n\n"
  )
})
knitr::opts_chunk$set(summary = "Show R code", message = FALSE)
library(highcharter)
library(dplyr)
hc_set_theme("hcrt", colors = hc_theme("smpl")$colors)
```

```{r gallery-layout, include=FALSE}
gallery <- function(types, draw) {
  charts <- lapply(types, function(type) {
    draw(type) |>
      hc_title(text = type, style = list(fontSize = "16px")) |>
      hc_legend(enabled = FALSE) |>
      hc_tooltip(outside = TRUE) |>
      hc_size(height = 235)
  })
  htmltools::div(class = "chart-grid", charts)
}
```

## Measurements and ranges

Each row is one day. Its position supplies `x`, `name` labels the day and
`y` is the mean temperature in °C. Columns rise from zero to the mean. A range column
extends from the day's `low` to its `high`. With these names, `hchart(temperatures, "columnrange")` reads the
columns directly. Use `hcaes(low = minimum, high = maximum)` if your
columns have different names.

```{r temperature-data, summary="Show temperature data"}
# fmt: skip
temperatures <- tibble::tribble(
  ~name, ~y, ~low, ~high,
  "Mon", 15,   12,    18,
  "Tue", 17,   13,    21,
  "Wed", 14,   11,    17,
  "Thu", 16,   12,    20,
  "Fri", 18,   14,    22
)
```

```{r temperature-gallery, summary="Show all temperature charts in R"}
gallery(
  c(
    "line",
    "spline",
    "area",
    "streamgraph",
    "areaspline",
    "column",
    "cylinder",
    "arearange",
    "areasplinerange",
    "columnrange",
    "errorbar",
    "dumbbell",
    "polar line",
    "polar column",
    "polar columnrange"
  ),
  function(label) {
    type <- sub("^polar ", "", label)
    hchart(
      temperatures,
      type,
      name = "Temperature",
      colorByPoint = TRUE,
      lineColor = "#2980b9",
      fillColor = "#2980b966",
      tooltip = list(valueSuffix = " °C")
    ) |>
      hc_chart(
        type = type,
        polar = startsWith(label, "polar"),
        options3d = list(enabled = type == "cylinder", alpha = 12, beta = 15)
      ) |>
      hc_xAxis(categories = temperatures$name) |>
      hc_yAxis(
        title = list(text = ""),
        min = if (type %in% c("column", "cylinder")) 0
      )
  }
)
```

## Quantities by category

Each visit appears once, at the last shopping step it reached (`name`).
Bars and slices show how the 100 visits ended (`y`). A funnel counts everyone
who reached each step: 100 viewed products, 42 added to cart, 30 started checkout
and 24 purchased. For variable-width columns and variable-radius slices, `z`
is the average cart value in Chilean pesos. Only visits with a cart have a value.

```{r shopping-data, summary="Show shopping data"}
# fmt: skip
shopping <- tibble::tribble(
  ~name,         ~y, ~z,
  "Viewed",      58, NA_real_,
  "Added",       12, 35000,
  "Checkout",     6, 50000,
  "Purchased",   24, 45000
)
```

```{r shopping-gallery, summary="Show all shopping charts in R"}
gallery(
  c(
    "bar",
    "column",
    "columnpyramid",
    "pie",
    "lollipop",
    "dotplot",
    "item",
    "waterfall",
    "variwide",
    "variablepie",
    "packedbubble",
    "treemap",
    "wordcloud",
    "funnel",
    "pyramid",
    "funnel3d",
    "pyramid3d"
  ),
  function(type) {
    points <- shopping
    if (type %in% c("variwide", "variablepie")) {
      points <- filter(points, !is.na(z))
    }
    if (type %in% c("funnel", "pyramid", "funnel3d", "pyramid3d")) {
      points$y <- rev(cumsum(rev(points$y)))
    }
    if (type %in% c("packedbubble", "treemap")) {
      points$value <- points$y
    }
    if (type == "wordcloud") {
      points$weight <- points$y
    }
    hchart(points, type, name = "Visits", colorByPoint = TRUE) |>
      hc_xAxis(categories = points$name) |>
      hc_chart(
        type = type,
        options3d = list(
          enabled = type %in% c("funnel3d", "pyramid3d"),
          alpha = 12,
          beta = 15
        )
      )
  }
)
```

## Relationships and hierarchies

Each row connects a parent team (`from`) to a subteam (`to`).
The link's `weight` is the subteam's headcount. Tree and sunburst charts
express the same hierarchy with `id` and `parent`.

```{r team-data, summary="Show team data"}
# fmt: skip
teams <- tibble::tribble(
  ~from,     ~to,       ~weight,
  "Studio",  "Design",       12,
  "Studio",  "Build",        18,
  "Design",  "Web",           7,
  "Design",  "Print",         5,
  "Build",   "Apps",         10,
  "Build",   "Data",          5,
  "Build",   "Tools",         3
)
```

```{r teams-gallery, summary="Show all team charts in R"}
gallery(
  c(
    "sankey",
    "dependencywheel",
    "arcdiagram",
    "networkgraph",
    "organization",
    "treegraph",
    "sunburst"
  ),
  function(type) {
    if (type %in% c("treegraph", "sunburst")) {
      nodes <- bind_rows(
        tibble(id = "Studio", name = "Studio"),
        transmute(teams, id = to, parent = from, name = to, value = weight)
      )
      if (type == "sunburst") {
        return(hchart(
          nodes,
          type,
          levels = list(list(level = 2, colorByPoint = TRUE))
        ))
      }
      return(hchart(nodes, type))
    }
    hchart(teams, type) |> hc_chart(inverted = type == "organization")
  }
)
```

For a network with an `igraph` layout, see the [igraph example](hchart.html#igraph-package).

## Positions, bubbles and wind

Each point is a South American capital at its longitude (`x`) and latitude (`y`).
Elevation in metres (`z`) sets bubble size or depth. For the illustrative
winds, `length` (vector) and `value` (wind barb) give the speed in m/s,
and `direction` gives the angle in degrees.

```{r capital-data, summary="Show capital data and wind colors"}
volcano_colors <- c("#000004", "#56106E", "#BB3754", "#F98C0A", "#FCFFA4")
# fmt: skip
capitals <- tibble::tribble(
  ~name,             ~x,     ~y, ~z, ~speed, ~direction,
  "Santiago",    -70.67, -33.45, 520,     5,        210,
  "Lima",        -77.04, -12.05, 150,     8,        180,
  "Brasília",    -47.88, -15.79, 1170,    3,         90,
  "Buenos Aires",-58.38, -34.60,  25,    11,        135
)
```

```{r capitals-gallery, summary="Show all capital charts in R"}
gallery(
  c("scatter", "bubble", "scatter3d", "vector", "windbarb", "polygon"),
  function(type) {
    points <- arrange(capitals, x)
    if (type == "polygon") {
      points <- points[chull(points$x, points$y), ]
    }
    if (type == "windbarb") {
      hc <- hchart(
        points,
        "scatter",
        id = "cities",
        marker = list(radius = 2)
      ) |>
        hc_add_series(
          points,
          "windbarb",
          hcaes(value = speed, color = colorize(speed, volcano_colors)),
          onSeries = "cities",
          yOffset = 0,
          name = "Wind"
        )
    } else if (type == "vector") {
      hc <- hchart(
        points,
        type,
        hcaes(length = speed, color = colorize(speed, volcano_colors)),
        vectorLength = 32,
        lineWidth = 2,
        name = "Wind"
      )
    } else {
      hc <- hchart(points, type, name = "Capitals")
    }
    hc |>
      hc_chart(
        type = if (type == "windbarb") "scatter" else type,
        options3d = list(
          enabled = type == "scatter3d",
          alpha = 15,
          beta = 20
        )
      ) |>
      hc_xAxis(min = -82, max = -43, title = list(text = "Longitude")) |>
      hc_yAxis(min = -40, max = -6, title = list(text = "Latitude"))
  }
)
```

## Gridded measurements

Each cell has a column (`x`), a row (`y`) and a measurement (`value`).
A heatmap colors rectangular cells, a tilemap uses hexagons, and a contour joins locations with the same value.

```{r grid-data}
cells <- expand.grid(x = 0:5, y = 0:5) |> mutate(value = sin(x) + cos(y))
```

```{r grid-types}
gallery(c("heatmap", "tilemap", "contour"), function(type) {
  hchart(cells, type) |>
    hc_colorAxis(
      min = -2,
      max = 2,
      stops = color_stops(colors = volcano_colors)
    )
})
```

## Other examples

Intervals use start and end positions. A Venn diagram sizes intersections by
`sets` and `value`, and a solid
gauge displays a single measurement (`y`).

### Comparing a measurement with a target

The bullet compares each daily mean (`y`) with a `target` of 18 °C.

```{r temperature-target}
hchart(temperatures, "bullet", hcaes(target = 18), colorByPoint = TRUE) |>
  hc_xAxis(categories = temperatures$name)
```

### Shopping timeline

A timeline places each event at its position (`x`) and labels it by `name`.
The four labels show the order of the shopping steps.

```{r shopping-timeline}
events <- shopping |> transmute(x = row_number() - 1L, name, label = name)
hchart(events, "timeline", name = "Shopping steps") |>
  hc_chart(type = "timeline")
```

### Task intervals

Each row spans two dates. Map the start to `x`, the end to `x2` and the lane's zero-based index to `y`.

```{r mapping-xrange}
tasks <- data.frame(
  start = base::as.Date(c("2025-01-06", "2025-01-08")),
  finish = base::as.Date(c("2025-01-09", "2025-01-13")),
  lane = 0:1
)
hchart(tasks, "xrange", hcaes(x = start, x2 = finish, y = lane)) |>
  hc_yAxis(categories = c("Design", "Review"))
```

```{r specialized-recipes, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
recipes <- c("venn", "solidgauge")
for (name in recipes) {
  path <- here::here("dev", "examples-charts", paste0(name, ".R"))
  cat(sub("(?m)^## ", "### ", knitr::spin_child(path), perl = TRUE), sep = "\n")
}
```

### Distributions

For a histogram in R, pass the result of `hist(..., plot = FALSE)` to
`hchart()`. See the [precomputed histogram example](hchart.html#precomputed-histograms).

A box plot reads five fields per group, `low`, `q1`, `median`, `q3` and `high`.

```{r mapping-boxplot}
waits <- data.frame(
  clinic = c("North", "South"),
  lower = c(4, 6),
  p25 = c(6, 8),
  p50 = c(10, 12),
  p75 = c(14, 15),
  upper = c(19, 22)
)
hchart(
  waits,
  "boxplot",
  hcaes(x = clinic, low = lower, q1 = p25, median = p50, q3 = p75, high = upper)
)
```

The `bellcurve` series fits a normal curve using the sample mean and standard
deviation. For a kernel density estimate, see [Densities](hchart.html#densities).

```{r bellcurve}
highchart() |>
  hc_add_series(
    type = "scatter",
    id = "scores",
    data = c(52, 58, 61, 63, 65, 67, 74),
    visible = FALSE,
    showInLegend = FALSE
  ) |>
  hc_add_series(
    type = "bellcurve",
    baseSeries = "scores",
    name = "Normal curve"
  )
```
